modules.title: Beginner SQL Foundations
modules.description: Master relational database basics, SELECT projections, WHERE filtering, DISTINCT, LIKE, ordering, and aggregation.

lessons.title: Introduction to Relational Databases & SELECT
lessons.concept: A relational database organizes data into tables consisting of rows and columns. The SELECT statement retrieves columns from a table.
lessons.expectedOutput: List of student IDs and their corresponding names.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Write a query to retrieve all columns from the students table.
hints: Use the asterisk (*) symbol to select all columns.
Make sure to specify FROM students;

lessons.title: Filtering Records with WHERE & Comparison Operators
lessons.concept: The WHERE clause filters records based on boolean conditions such as =, >, <, >=, <=, and <>.
lessons.syntax: SELECT column1 FROM table_name WHERE condition;
lessons.example: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks >= 80;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Find all students who have marks strictly greater than 75.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 75;

lessons.title: Sorting and Limiting with ORDER BY & LIMIT
lessons.concept: ORDER BY sorts the returned records in ASC (ascending) or DESC (descending) order. LIMIT restricts the number of rows returned.
lessons.syntax: SELECT column1 FROM table_name ORDER BY column1 DESC LIMIT n;
lessons.example: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC LIMIT 3;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select the top 2 students sorted alphabetically by name.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 2;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 2;

lessons.title: Removing Duplicates with DISTINCT
lessons.concept: The DISTINCT keyword eliminates duplicate rows from the result set so each unique value appears only once.
lessons.expectedOutput: Unique student IDs that have at least one enrolment.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select all unique academic terms from the enrolments table.
hints: Query the term column from enrolments

lessons.title: Pattern Matching with LIKE & Wildcards
lessons.concept: The LIKE operator searches for a specified pattern in a text column using % (zero or more characters) and _ (single character).
lessons.syntax: SELECT column1 FROM table_name WHERE column1 LIKE '%pattern%';
lessons.example: SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE title LIKE '%Archive%';
lessons.expectedOutput: Books whose title contains the word Archive.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Find the id and title of books whose title contains the word 'Index'.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE title LIKE '%Index%';
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE title LIKE '%Index%';

lessons.title: Basic Aggregate Functions (COUNT, AVG, MAX)
lessons.concept: Aggregate functions perform a calculation across a set of rows and return a single summary value.
lessons.syntax: SELECT COUNT(*), AVG(col), MAX(col) FROM table_name;
lessons.example: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, MIN(marks) AS lowest FROM students;
lessons.expectedOutput: Total count and lowest student mark.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Calculate total_students, average marks rounded to 2 decimals (avg_marks), and highest mark (top_mark) from students.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students, ROUND(AVG(marks), 2) AS avg_marks, MAX(marks) AS top_mark FROM students;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_students, ROUND(AVG(marks), 2) AS avg_marks, MAX(marks) AS top_mark FROM students;

modules.title: Joins, Aggregations & Subqueries
modules.description: Connect related tables with INNER and LEFT JOINs, calculate summary metrics with GROUP BY, HAVING, UNION, and subqueries.

lessons.title: Connecting Tables with INNER JOIN
lessons.concept: An INNER JOIN selects records that have matching values in both tables based on a foreign key relationship.
lessons.syntax: SELECT t1.col, t2.col FROM table1 t1 INNER JOIN table2 t2 ON t1.id = t2.ref_id;
lessons.example: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id INNER JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id;
lessons.expectedOutput: Student names paired with the title of each course they are taking.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select student name and their enrolment term by joining students and enrolments.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT s.name, e.term FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT s.name, e.term FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id;

lessons.title: Preserving Unmatched Rows with LEFT JOIN
lessons.concept: A LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table, filling NULL when no match exists.
lessons.syntax: SELECT a.col, b.col FROM left_table a LEFT JOIN right_table b ON a.id = b.a_id;
lessons.example: SELECT d.name, e.name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id;
lessons.expectedOutput: Every department, including Operations which has NULL for employee.
lessons.exercisePrompt: List all department names (as department) and employee names (as employee) ordered by d.id, e.id.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT d.name AS department, e.name AS employee FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id ORDER BY d.id, e.id;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT d.name AS department, e.name AS employee FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id ORDER BY d.id, e.id;
hints: Start from departments d and LEFT JOIN employees e

lessons.title: Summarizing Data with GROUP BY & HAVING
lessons.concept: GROUP BY aggregates rows that have the same values into summary rows. HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
lessons.syntax: SELECT category, COUNT(*), AVG(val) FROM table GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
lessons.example: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(salary) as avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
lessons.expectedOutput: Number of employees and average salary per department.
lessons.exercisePrompt: List department_id and average salary for departments with average salary above 75000.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) as avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 75000;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) as avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 75000;

lessons.title: Subqueries and Nested Expressions
lessons.concept: A subquery is a query nested inside another query, used in WHERE clauses or column projections.
lessons.syntax: SELECT col FROM table WHERE val > (SELECT AVG(val) FROM table);
lessons.example: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
lessons.expectedOutput: Employees whose salary is higher than the overall company average.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Find employees who earn more than the overall average salary.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
hints: Use (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) as the comparator in the WHERE clause.

lessons.title: Combining Result Sets with UNION
lessons.concept: UNION combines the result sets of two or more SELECT statements into a single result set (UNION removes duplicates; UNION ALL keeps all rows).
lessons.syntax: SELECT col FROM table1 UNION ALL SELECT col FROM table2;
lessons.example: SELECT name FROM authors UNION SELECT name FROM members;
lessons.expectedOutput: Combined list of all author and member names.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Combine all authors and members with a role column ('Author' or 'Member'), ordered by role, name.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, 'Author' AS role FROM authors UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Member' AS role FROM members ORDER BY role, name;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, 'Author' AS role FROM authors UNION ALL SELECT name, 'Member' AS role FROM members ORDER BY role, name;
hints: Ensure both SELECT statements have the same number of columns

lessons.title: Range Filtering with BETWEEN & IN
lessons.concept: BETWEEN checks whether a value lies within an inclusive range, and IN checks whether a value matches any item in a list.
lessons.syntax: SELECT col FROM table WHERE col BETWEEN low AND high;
lessons.example: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE id IN (1, 3);
lessons.exercisePrompt: Find id, name, and marks of students whose marks are BETWEEN 80 AND 95, ordered by marks descending.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT id, name, marks FROM students WHERE marks BETWEEN 80 AND 95 ORDER BY marks DESC;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT id, name, marks FROM students WHERE marks BETWEEN 80 AND 95 ORDER BY marks DESC;

modules.title: Advanced SQL & Performance
modules.description: Common Table Expressions (CTEs), Window Functions, Query Optimization, Normalization, and Transactions.

lessons.title: Common Table Expressions (WITH Clause)
lessons.concept: Common Table Expressions (CTEs) define temporary named result sets that can be referenced within a SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement.
lessons.syntax: WITH cte_name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM cte_name;
lessons.example: WITH OrderTotals AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price_cents) AS total_cents FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT * FROM OrderTotals WHERE total_cents > 1000;
lessons.expectedOutput: Orders whose line-item total exceeds 1000 cents.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Create a CTE named OrderTotals to calculate total_cents per order_id from order_items and select all rows from it.
lessons.solutionSql: WITH OrderTotals AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price_cents) AS total_cents FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) SELECT * FROM OrderTotals;
hints: Query the CTE with SELECT * FROM OrderTotals;

lessons.title: Window Functions (RANK, ROW_NUMBER)
lessons.concept: Window functions perform calculations across a set of table rows that are related to the current row, without collapsing rows like GROUP BY.
lessons.syntax: SELECT col, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;
lessons.example: SELECT name, salary, department_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) as rank FROM employees;
lessons.expectedOutput: Employees ranked by salary within their respective departments.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select employee name, salary and row number ordered by salary descending.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) as row_num FROM employees;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) as row_num FROM employees;
hints: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC)

lessons.title: Partitioned Window Aggregates
lessons.concept: Aggregate functions like SUM() and AVG() can be paired with OVER (PARTITION BY ...) to display group totals alongside each individual row.
lessons.syntax: SELECT col, SUM(val) OVER (PARTITION BY group_col) FROM table;
lessons.example: SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER () AS company_avg FROM employees;
lessons.expectedOutput: Each employee paired with the company average salary.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Show each employee's name, department_id, salary, and their department's total salary (dept_total_salary), ordered by department_id, salary DESC.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, department_id, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_total_salary FROM employees ORDER BY department_id, salary DESC;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, department_id, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_total_salary FROM employees ORDER BY department_id, salary DESC;

lessons.title: Query Optimization & Index-Friendly Projections
lessons.concept: Selecting only needed columns instead of SELECT * and filtering on indexed primary/foreign keys reduces I/O and speeds up execution.
lessons.syntax: SELECT t1.col, t2.col FROM t1 INNER JOIN t2 ON t1.fk = t2.pk WHERE t1.pk = ?;
lessons.example: SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE id = 1;
lessons.expectedOutput: Direct primary-key lookup without scanning unneeded columns.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Project product name, quantity, and unit_price_cents for order_id = 1 by joining order_items and products, ordered by p.id.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT p.name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price_cents FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE oi.order_id = 1 ORDER BY p.id;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT p.name, oi.quantity, oi.unit_price_cents FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.id WHERE oi.order_id = 1 ORDER BY p.id;

lessons.title: Transactions & ACID Guarantees
lessons.concept: Transactions bundle multiple database operations into an atomic unit with COMMIT and ROLLBACK.
lessons.example: BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE products SET price_cents = price_cents + 100 WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select id, name, and price_cents from products where price_cents > 0 ordered by id.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT id, name, price_cents FROM products WHERE price_cents > 0 ORDER BY id;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT id, name, price_cents FROM products WHERE price_cents > 0 ORDER BY id;
hints: Select id, name, price_cents from products.

lessons.title: Database Normalization & Multi-Table Foreign Keys
lessons.concept: Third Normal Form (3NF) eliminates redundant data by splitting entities into normalized tables linked by foreign keys.
lessons.syntax: SELECT ... FROM child JOIN parent ON ... JOIN grandparent ON ...;
lessons.example: SELECT b.title, a.name FROM books b INNER JOIN authors a ON b.author_id = a.id;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Reconstruct full loan details (loan_id, book title, author_name, member_name) by joining loans, books, authors, and members ordered by l.id.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT l.id AS loan_id, b.title, a.name AS author_name, m.name AS member_name FROM loans l INNER JOIN books b ON l.book_id = b.id INNER JOIN authors a ON b.author_id = a.id INNER JOIN members m ON l.member_id = m.id ORDER BY l.id;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT l.id AS loan_id, b.title, a.name AS author_name, m.name AS member_name FROM loans l INNER JOIN books b ON l.book_id = b.id INNER JOIN authors a ON b.author_id = a.id INNER JOIN members m ON l.member_id = m.id ORDER BY l.id;
hints: Join loans -> books -> authors and loans -> members

challenges.title: High Honor Roll Students
challenges.description: Find all students who scored above 85 marks. Return name and marks ordered from highest marks to lowest marks.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 85 ORDER BY marks DESC;

challenges.title: Library Book Catalogue
challenges.description: Select the id and title of all books in the library catalogue, sorted alphabetically by title.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT id, title FROM books ORDER BY ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT id, title FROM books ORDER BY title ASC;
hints: Select id and title from books
Sort with ORDER BY title ASC

challenges.title: Affordable Store Products
challenges.description: Find all products priced under 2000 cents ($20.00). Return name and price_cents ordered from lowest price to highest.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, price_cents FROM products WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, price_cents FROM products WHERE price_cents < 2000 ORDER BY price_cents ASC;
hints: Sort with ORDER BY price_cents ASC

challenges.title: Top-Level Managers
challenges.description: Find all employees who do not report to any manager (manager_id IS NULL). Return id, name, and salary ordered by salary descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT id, name, salary FROM employees WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT id, name, salary FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL ORDER BY salary DESC;
hints: Use IS NULL (not = NULL) to check manager_id

challenges.title: Distinct Enrolment Terms
challenges.description: Retrieve all unique academic terms from the enrolments table, ordered alphabetically.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT DISTINCT ... FROM enrolments ORDER BY ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT term FROM enrolments ORDER BY term ASC;
hints: Sort with ORDER BY term ASC

challenges.title: Returned Book Loans
challenges.description: Find all loans that have already been returned (returned_on IS NOT NULL). Return id, book_id, member_id, and returned_on ordered by id ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT id, book_id, member_id, returned_on FROM loans WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT id, book_id, member_id, returned_on FROM loans WHERE returned_on IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id ASC;
hints: Use WHERE returned_on IS NOT NULL

challenges.title: Bulk Order Line Items
challenges.description: Find all order_items where quantity is 2 or more. Return order_id, product_id, and quantity ordered by product_id ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity FROM order_items WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity FROM order_items WHERE quantity >= 2 ORDER BY product_id ASC;

challenges.title: Course Enrolment Roster
challenges.description: List each student's name, the title of the course they are enrolled in, and the enrolment term. Order by student name ascending, then course title ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.term FROM students s ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.term FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id INNER JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id ORDER BY s.name ASC, c.title ASC;
hints: Join students with enrolments on s.id = e.student_id
Order by s.name ASC, c.title ASC

challenges.title: Top Earners by Department
challenges.description: Find all employees who have a salary of 75000 or greater and belong to a non-null department. Return name, salary, and department_id ordered by salary descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees WHERE salary >= 75000 AND department_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY salary DESC;

challenges.title: Department Headcount & Average Salary
challenges.description: For every department (including departments with zero employees), return department name, headcount, and average salary rounded to 2 decimal places. Order by headcount descending, then department name ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM departments d ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY headcount DESC, d.name ASC;
hints: Use LEFT JOIN so departments without employees are included
Use COUNT(e.id) instead of COUNT(*) so empty departments show 0

challenges.title: Books and Their Authors
challenges.description: Return each book's title alongside its author's name (aliased as author_name), sorted alphabetically by book title.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT b.title, a.name AS author_name FROM books b ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT b.title, a.name AS author_name FROM books b INNER JOIN authors a ON b.author_id = a.id ORDER BY b.title ASC;
hints: Join books with authors on b.author_id = a.id

challenges.title: Product Units Sold
challenges.description: Calculate total units sold for each product that has been ordered. Return product name and total quantity aliased as units_sold, ordered by units_sold descending, then product name ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT p.name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p INNER JOIN order_items oi ON p.id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY units_sold DESC, p.name ASC;
hints: Join products with order_items on p.id = oi.product_id

challenges.title: Direct Reports & Their Managers
challenges.description: Using a self-join on employees, list every employee who has a manager. Return employee_name, manager_name, and the employee's salary, ordered by employee_name ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, m.name AS manager_name, e.salary FROM employees e ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, m.name AS manager_name, e.salary FROM employees e INNER JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id ORDER BY e.name ASC;
hints: Join employees e with employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id

challenges.title: Course Enrolment Counts
challenges.description: For each course, return its title and the number of enrolled students (enrolled_count). Order by enrolled_count descending, then course title ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT c.title, COUNT(e.student_id) AS enrolled_count FROM courses c ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.title, COUNT(e.student_id) AS enrolled_count FROM courses c LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON c.id = e.course_id GROUP BY c.id, c.title ORDER BY enrolled_count DESC, c.title ASC;
hints: Use LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON c.id = e.course_id

challenges.title: Customer Order Revenue
challenges.description: Calculate each ordering customer's total expenditure in dollars from order_items (quantity * unit_price_cents / 100.0). Return customer name and total_spent rounded to 2 decimal places, ordered by total_spent descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT c.name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) / 100.0, 2) AS total_spent FROM customers c ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) / 100.0, 2) AS total_spent FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id INNER JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

challenges.title: Open & Unreturned Loans
challenges.description: List all active loans where returned_on IS NULL. Return member name, book title, and loaned_on date, ordered by loaned_on ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT m.name, b.title, l.loaned_on FROM loans l ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT m.name, b.title, l.loaned_on FROM loans l INNER JOIN members m ON l.member_id = m.id INNER JOIN books b ON l.book_id = b.id WHERE l.returned_on IS NULL ORDER BY l.loaned_on ASC;
hints: Join loans with members and books

challenges.title: Unenrolled Students
challenges.description: Find all students who are not enrolled in any course yet. Return id, name, and marks ordered by id ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT s.id, s.name, s.marks FROM students s ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT s.id, s.name, s.marks FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id WHERE e.student_id IS NULL ORDER BY s.id ASC;
hints: Use LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id
Filter with WHERE e.student_id IS NULL

challenges.title: Above-Average Earners
challenges.description: Using a subquery, find all employees whose salary is strictly greater than the company-wide average salary. Return name and salary ordered by salary descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (...)
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY salary DESC;

challenges.title: Department Salary Ranking (Window)
challenges.description: Rank employees within their own department by salary descending using RANK(). Return employee name, department_name, salary, and dept_rank ordered by department_name ascending, dept_rank ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department_name, e.salary, RANK() OVER (...) AS dept_rank FROM employees e ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department_name, e.salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS dept_rank FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id ORDER BY d.name ASC, dept_rank ASC;
hints: Use RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.department_id ORDER BY e.salary DESC)
Join departments d ON e.department_id = d.id

challenges.title: Authors With No Open Loans
challenges.description: Find all authors who currently have zero unreturned (open) book loans using NOT EXISTS. Return author id and name ordered by id ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT a.id, a.name FROM authors a WHERE NOT EXISTS (...)
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT a.id, a.name FROM authors a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM books b INNER JOIN loans l ON b.id = l.book_id WHERE b.author_id = a.id AND l.returned_on IS NULL) ORDER BY a.id ASC;
hints: Inside NOT EXISTS, join books and loans where b.author_id = a.id AND l.returned_on IS NULL
